onboarding.title: Welcome to PyroStudio
onboarding.subtitle: Step {{current}} of {{total}} · {{step}}
onboarding.step1Intro: A workspace is a folder with your connections (without passwords), saved queries, favorites, and snippets. It lets you version with git, share with your team, or separate projects.
onboarding.noWorkspaceNote: Without a workspace, everything is stored locally on this machine. You can create one later from the sidebar.
onboarding.step2Intro: Passwords are never stored in the UI or the workspace: they go into an encrypted vault (AES-256-GCM) on this machine, with its master key stored in your OS keychain.
onboarding.vaultKeychain: The master key is stored in the system keychain.
onboarding.vaultFallback: No system keychain available: the master key is stored in a protected file (master.key, 0600 permissions). Reason: {{reason}}
onboarding.step3Intro: Create your first connection to MariaDB, MySQL, or SQLite. You can mark it as production (reinforced confirmations) or read-only. You can reopen this introduction anytime from Preferences → About.
onboarding.demoBody: explore PyroStudio with a sample SQLite database (a store with customers, orders, and products). It is created in the app data folder only if you request it.

workspaceSettings.title: Workspace
workspaceSettings.subtitle: Save connections and queries in a folder you can sync across devices (for example, a Google Drive desktop folder).
workspaceSettings.unavailableNote: Empty lists are not shown and nothing is saved elsewhere. If the folder moved or the sync drive is not mounted yet, locate it again or retry.
workspaceSettings.exportTooltip: .pyrows package with connections, queries, folders, and snippets; never includes passwords
workspaceSettings.exportSuccessMessage: Packaged {{files}} file(s) without passwords. Anyone importing it will need to enter credentials on their machine.
workspaceSettings.importTooltip: Choose a .pyrows package and an empty folder to create the workspace
workspaceSettings.useLocalMessage: PyroStudio will switch back to connections and queries stored only on this machine. The workspace folder is not modified or deleted.
workspaceSettings.createDescription: Choose an empty folder (for example inside Google Drive 'My Drive'). If it already contains a workspace, use 'Open workspace'.
workspaceSettings.migrationAlreadyDone: Local data has already been imported into this workspace. Repeating the import is safe: it does not duplicate items.
workspaceSettings.migrationPending: There are {{connections}} connections and {{queries}} queries stored only on this machine.
workspaceSettings.migrationConfirmMessage: {{connections}} connections and {{queries}} saved queries will be copied to the workspace folder.
workspaceSettings.migrationConfirmDetails: Passwords and tokens are NOT copied: they remain in this machine's encrypted vault. Original data is not deleted. Existing items with different content are not overwritten and will be reported as conflicts. You can safely repeat the import.
workspaceSettings.sharedItem1: Connection definitions (host, port, user, TLS, SSH, HTTP tunnel)
workspaceSettings.localOnlyItem1: Passwords, tokens, and AI keys (local encrypted vault)
workspaceSettings.syncFootnote: When opening the workspace on another machine, connections appear as 'Credentials pending on this machine' until you enter the password. Sync depends on your provider (e.g. Google Drive); if two machines edit the same query at once, PyroStudio detects the change and asks before overwriting.

database.longTxDescription: With auto-commit disabled, the transaction bar warns after staying open this long with uncommitted changes (holds locks on modified rows).
database.csvSplitBefore: When exporting to CSV or CSV.gz, split the output into numbered files (
database.noPkDescription: Define how PyroStudio should behave when you try to edit or delete rows in a table without a primary key.
database.noPkFullRowMiddle: as the unique identifier criteria with
database.noPkFullRowAfter: . Enables interactive and safe editing and deletion in the data grid.
database.noPkBlockDescription: Strictly blocks any edit or deletion in tables without a primary key to prevent accidental ambiguous modifications.
database.safeModeDescription: Intercepts and requires interactive confirmation for destructive statements such as DROP, TRUNCATE, and DELETE/UPDATE without a WHERE clause.
database.prodConfirmDescription: Shows a high-risk visual warning before connecting or executing changes on servers tagged PROD.
database.infiniteScrollDescription: Loads rows progressively in dynamic chunks as you scroll down using indexed keyset pagination.
